questions.q: Why does a single tempdb data file become a bottleneck under high concurrency?
options: Many sessions creating and dropping temp objects contend for the same allocation pages within that one file, visible as PAGELATCH waits
tempdb has a hard row-count limit per file
A single file causes tempdb to switch to SIMPLE recovery automatically
tempdb cannot grow past a single file's maximum size
questions.explain: tempdb's allocation pages track free space; under heavy concurrent temp-object creation, contention on those pages within one file shows up as PAGELATCH waits.

questions.q: What is Microsoft's current recommendation for tempdb data files?
options: Multiple data files, all the same initial size and growth setting, one per logical CPU up to a maximum of 8
Exactly one large data file regardless of CPU count
One file per user database on the instance
As many files as possible, sized differently to fill available disk space
questions.explain: SQL Server Setup itself has configured multiple equally-sized tempdb files this way automatically since SQL Server 2016, one per logical core up to 8.

questions.q: Why must tempdb's multiple data files be the same size and growth setting?
options: SQL Server's proportional-fill algorithm allocates more to whichever file has proportionally more free space, so uneven files defeat the purpose of splitting
Unequal file sizes cause SQL Server to refuse to start
It's only a cosmetic recommendation with no functional effect
Equal sizing is required only for the log file, not tempdb data files
questions.explain: Proportional fill directs more new allocations to files with more free space; if files are unequal, contention concentrates back onto fewer files, undoing the benefit of splitting.

questions.q: Once an instance has more than 8 logical CPUs, what's the recommended approach to adding more tempdb files?
options: Add more files in multiples of 4, but only after monitoring shows continued allocation-page contention
Automatically add one file per additional core with no monitoring
Never exceed 8 files under any circumstances
Switch to a single very large file instead
questions.explain: Beyond 8 cores, Microsoft's guidance is to add tempdb files in increments of 4 only if monitoring still shows PAGELATCH contention, not to automatically scale with core count.

questions.q: Why is Instant File Initialization especially valuable for tempdb?
options: tempdb is recreated fresh on every SQL Server restart and is one of the most frequently-growing databases, so skipping zero-initialization saves real time
IFI is required for tempdb to support row versioning
IFI applies only to the tempdb log file
tempdb cannot grow at all without IFI enabled
questions.explain: Because tempdb is rebuilt every restart and grows often on a busy instance, IFI's speedup on data file creation and growth events is especially valuable there — though it still doesn't apply to the log file.
